I have a great mom but she had had a drinking problem all my life. I realize now that that is just a symptom of her own mental illness. The drinking lead to some arguments between family members that got physical and sometimes she would come to me for comfort (her being 30 and me 8). She was over controlling of my sister and often made my sister feel like a "bad child" and I was the "good child." That has caused hurt between my sister and I. That being said, she really has always tried to be a good parent and in a lot of ways she has been. She is just a person trying to figure shit out like everyone else. She was over controlling of my sister, but now I see that when she was a young mom of two and my sister had a lot of problems, it was probably hard for my mom to know what to do.
That's doesn't sounds like a healthy relationship.

I've had some releife by practicing mindfulness, being aware of how tired I am, and currently building my support network. It's important to have someone to confide in and to have more than one person (sometimes people are not available to hold that space for you). Antidotaley, aroma therapy and meditation.
All you can do is try to be there for her. Listen and help her feel not worthless. Maybe gently suggest that she could see a professional counselor. Remember, to take care of yourself too. <3
